findings.title: Personal OAuth sessions export ~/.claude-derived session content
findings.what: D2 captures all session-generated artifact types and ships classified session-data to push-ingest, while D3 introduces the personal-OAuth path. Refusing only the secret class and proving only that .credentials.json is excluded does not satisfy ADR 0008's stricter invariant that a subscription OAuth credential must never send ~/.claude content.
findings.fix: Make the credential kind an explicit shipper policy input and fail closed: when the dispatch uses personal/subscription OAuth, prohibit all ~/.claude-derived egress rather than merely excluding secret-classified files. Use an enterprise API credential for telemetry-exporting dispatches, or keep subscription-authenticated artifacts local.
findings.acceptance: An end-to-end test provisions a personal/subscription-OAuth RemoteSession with representative config, transcript, history, and credential files under ~/.claude, exercises the shipper, and asserts zero bytes and zero artifact metadata from ~/.claude reach push-ingest; a separate enterprise-API test proves permitted session-data still ships.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the same plan explicitly combines the personal-OAuth path at lines 108-110 with export of session-data at lines 103-107 and 117-120. The stated safeguard covers the secret class/.credentials.json only, so it does not cover the broader ~/.claude-content prohibition.

findings.title: Push-ingest ships without a measurable resource budget
findings.what: The plan adds a multi-host push-ingest endpoint that feeds the existing parse and SQLite cache pipeline, but gives no payload/concurrency bounds, backpressure behavior, or latency and peak-memory probe. Signature gating establishes idempotency, not a performance envelope.
findings.fix: Add a representative push-ingest benchmark/probe and explicit maximum request size, concurrency/backpressure policy, p95 ingestion-latency budget, and peak-memory budget; make the relevant gate fail when those limits regress.
findings.acceptance: CI submits a documented representative multi-host artifact batch at the supported concurrency, asserts request-size rejection/backpressure behavior, and verifies p95 ingestion latency and peak RSS remain within the plan's declared budgets.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of lines 95-102 confirmed that the only controls named for the new endpoint are signature-gated idempotency and reuse of the parse/SQLite-cache pipeline. No probe, resource bound, latency budget, or backpressure acceptance criterion appears in the dispatched document.
